$comment: The method table: every request, notification and error code of the daemon-client contract, naming types from contract/schema. contractVersion marks only breaking changes: raise it when a method, field or error code is removed or renamed, a field changes type or becomes required, or a meaning changes. Additive changes keep it. stableCore entries never change at all. callableBy lists the client kinds that may send a request; needsPerson marks requests the daemon runs only after a person said yes (some only in some cases, as their doc says); leased marks requests that take the brick's write lease for exactly their own length.

hello/start.doc: Open the hello: the client's nonce and who it is; the daemon answers with its nonce and its proof.

hello/finish.doc: Finish the hello with the client's proof; any other request before this one closes the connection.

daemon/status.doc: The daemon, its clients (with the brick each shows) and the bricks it holds.

daemon/exit.doc: Ask the daemon to end once no write is in progress. A newer release client, or a development client meeting a release daemon, replaces it without asking anyone; any other request is a restart and runs only after a person said yes.

log/notice.doc: A notification a client showed a person, for the daemon's log.

bricks/list.doc: Every brick the daemon knows; with waitForDiscovery, after the first discovery round.

bricks/connect.doc: Connect a brick for this client, pairing on the way; hold keeps it past this client; reuse takes a brick connected already as it is, only adding this client as a holder.

bricks/disconnect.doc: Drop this client's hold; forEveryone signs the brick out whoever holds it.

bricks/storage.doc: Total and free space on the brick.

bricks/pair.doc: Pair over Bluetooth; the person confirms on the brick.

bricks/forget.doc: Unpair on this computer and on the brick, after a person said yes.

bricks/clearBluetoothList.doc: Remove the entries of the brick's list of paired devices, after a person said yes.

files/list.doc: The entries of a folder on the brick.

files/exists.doc: Whether a path exists on the brick.

files/size.doc: The size of a file or a folder on the brick.

files/read.doc: Read a file: to a local path the daemon writes, inline as base64 in the answer, or into a transfer handle the client then drains with transfer/read. A local file already there is replaced unless replace is false.

files/follow.doc: Hear files/appended for a file on the brick as it grows, from fromOffset on, until subscriptions/cancel or files/followEnded. file_not_found when the file is not there yet; at most two follows per brick, for every client together.

files/write.doc: Write a file: from a local path, from a filled transfer handle, or from inline base64 content. A file already there is replaced unless replace is false.

files/makeDirectory.doc: Make a folder on the brick.

files/remove.doc: Remove a file or a folder.

files/removePaths.doc: Remove several paths under one lease.

files/move.doc: Move or rename a file on the brick. Something already at the target is replaced unless replace is false.

transfer/begin.doc: Open an upload buffer of size bytes.

transfer/write.doc: Append base64 data to an upload buffer.

transfer/read.doc: Take the next chunk of a download; done with the last one.

programs/deployAndRun.doc: Check nothing runs, upload the files, start the program: one lease, released at the verified start.

programs/run.doc: Start a program already on the brick; replace stops one that runs.

programs/stop.doc: Stop the running program; never waits for a lease.

programs/emergencyStop.doc: Stop the program and the motors; never waits for a lease.

programs/status.doc: The program state now, or once it changes within waitMs.

programs/subscribe.doc: Hear programs/stateChanged for a brick, across reconnects.

shell/run.doc: Run a shell command on the brick; only with access full.

settings/list.doc: Every setting with its rules and value.

settings/set.doc: Change a setting; a dangerous one changes only after a person said yes.

telemetry/rows.doc: Every telemetry row a client can subscribe to.

telemetry/subscribe.doc: Hear telemetry/update for rows of a brick, with a snapshot first.

telemetry/foreground.doc: The brick whose telemetry this client shows in the foreground; daemon/status names it as the client's shows, and a change reaches every client as daemon/showsChanged.

subscriptions/cancel.doc: End any subscription by its id; an id is valid on its own connection only.

bricks/changed.doc: The whole brick list, whenever anything in it changes.

bricks/reconnected.doc: A brick has a route again: after it was lost, and also when it is first connected. Subscriptions on it carry on.

bricks/pairingStarted.doc: A pairing started, whoever asked for it.

bricks/pairingEvent.doc: One step of a running pairing.

bricks/oneSidedRepair.doc: The brick paired one-sidedly and the cockpit repaired it.

telemetry/update.doc: New telemetry values for a subscription.

files/appended.doc: A followed file grew: the bytes it grew by, in order.

files/followEnded.doc: A follow ended without a subscriptions/cancel, and why.

question/withdrawn.doc: A question this client was asked is no longer open.

daemon/showsChanged.doc: The brick a client shows changed: it showed another or none, or it left while showing one. Carries every client as daemon/status names it.

question/ask.doc: The daemon asks a client with a person at it; a client without a person answers keep.

brick.doc: The brick, its transport or the work on it failed.

lease.doc: Another client holds the brick's write lease.

person.doc: The operation needs a person's answer.

daemon.doc: The daemon could not serve the request, or the outcome is unknown.

request.doc: The request was malformed or named something the daemon does not have.

connection_failed.doc: The connection to the brick could not be made.

timeout.doc: The brick did not answer in time.

protocol_failed.doc: The brick's answer did not make sense.

heartbeat_failed.doc: The brick stopped answering the heartbeat.

no_provider.doc: No transport serves the requested channel.

invalid_transition.doc: The session cannot do that in its current state.

channel_changed.doc: The brick's channel changed during the operation.

queue_unavailable.doc: The brick's command queue is closed.

consumer_failed.doc: A consumer of the brick's data failed.

subscription_failed.doc: The subscription could not be made.

program_running.doc: A program runs on the brick already.

program_not_found.doc: No such program on the brick.

file_not_found.doc: No such file on the brick.

mode_conflict.doc: A sensor port is claimed in another mode.

access_denied.doc: The access mode, or this client's kind, does not allow it; the message says which.

brick_ambiguous.doc: A brick name matched several bricks; data.candidates lists them.

brick_not_found.doc: No brick matches the name or id.

brick_unreachable.doc: The brick never answered: switched off, out of range, or its radio is off.

link_lost.doc: A link that worked dropped during the operation.

backend_unavailable.doc: The operating system's Bluetooth or USB stack is not available.

device_permission.doc: The operating system refused access to the device.

brick_busy.doc: Another client holds the brick's write lease; data.holder names it.

needs_person.doc: The operation needs a person's answer, and no client with a person could be asked; data.command is what a person can run.

daemon_unavailable.doc: The daemon is not reachable, could not start, or went away during the call.

outcome_unknown.doc: The daemon went away during a call that changes a brick; whether it took effect is unknown. Do not retry blindly.

replay_unmatched.doc: A replay daemon has no recorded reply left for the request: the recording is stale.

cancelled.doc: The caller, a stop or the daemon cancelled the operation.

file_exists.doc: The target is there already, and the request asked not to replace it.

invalid_request.doc: The request was malformed or named something the daemon does not have.

internal.doc: Anything else; the message says what.
